finding: EXPANDED VALIDATION (n=36, supersedes the n=10 cfg-interval.json recommendation): cfg_interval 0-0.2 keeps -20.6% speedup with no detectable quality loss (paired t=+0.26, CI ±2.57); cfg_interval 0.7-1.0 shows a SIGNIFICANT quality regression (-6.06, t=-3.19, p=0.003; Quality and Aesthetics individually significant). Recommendation changed from v3 to v2.
why_the_n10_verdict_changed: The n=10 prompt set (CI ±5.5 on the total delta) could not resolve V3's true effect and under-sampled the content types V3 damages most. The n=36 set (10 originals kept byte-identical by generation determinism + 26 stratified additions; Q/A/Al=36, RWF=24, CG=21) resolves it.

method.generation: same as cfg-interval.json but over gen36-prompts.jsonl (36 prompts, same seeds 1000+ID, 2048x2048, 50 steps); runs 2026-08-25 13:11-20:36 UTC, zero interruptions
method.determinism_crosscheck: the 10 original IDs' images are sha256 byte-identical to the n=10 run in all three sets (30/30 pairs) - old and new evidence directly corroborate
method.quality: same judge and official params as cfg-interval.json; 153 tasks per set, 0 parse failures across all three sets
method.stats: per-prompt paired t-tests, two aggregation conventions (flat leaf-mean and bench hierarchical) - verdicts identical under both; independently recomputed by a separate verifier (max deviation <=0.01)

v2_cfg_interval_0_0.2.verdict: no detectable quality loss; CI tight

v3_cfg_interval_0.7_1.0.verdict: RETRACTED: significant quality cost; do not use as default

environment: single gfx1100 48GB, bf16, vram_mode balanced, sdpa; judge int8 on same host (CPU vision tower)
